CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Nurse Assistant Certification Training Program (NATP): minimum 160 hours total - 60 hours classroom theory + 100 hours supervised clinical training

CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Pre-Contact Training (16 hours required before any direct resident contact): communications and interpersonal skills; infection control; safety and emergency procedures including Heimlich maneuver; promoting residents' independence; respecting residents' rights
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: These 5 topic areas are both state (22 CCR §71835) and federal (42 CFR §483.152(b)(1)) requirements. Must be completed before student may have any contact with a resident.

CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Module 1 - Introduction (2 hrs theory): role and responsibilities of the CNA; Title 22 Division 5 CCR overview; requirements for nurse assistant certification; professionalism; ethics and confidentiality
Module 2 - Patients' Rights (2 hrs theory / 1 hr clinical): resident rights as specified in 22 CCR §72527 and HSC §§1599.1, 1599.2, 1599.3 and 42 CFR §§483.10, 483.12, 483.13, 483.15
Module 3 - Body Mechanics (2 hrs theory / 3 hrs clinical): proper body mechanics; use of assistive devices; safe patient handling and transfer techniques

Module 4 - Infection Control (2 hrs theory / 3 hrs clinical): standard precautions; universal precautions; methods to handle patients and materials soiled with blood/body fluids; reducing transmission of infectious agents
Module 5 - Safety and Emergency Care (3 hrs theory / 3 hrs clinical): fall prevention; fire safety; emergency procedures; Heimlich maneuver; CPR awareness
Module 6 - Personal Care (6 hrs theory / 20 hrs clinical): bathing; oral hygiene; grooming; dressing; skin care; toileting; perineal care; continence care
Module 7 - Nutrition and Fluid Balance (4 hrs theory / 10 hrs clinical): assisting with meals; feeding techniques; nutritional needs; fluid intake and output measurement; dysphagia awareness
Module 8 - Musculoskeletal and Integumentary Care (4 hrs theory / 10 hrs clinical): skin observation; pressure ulcer prevention; range of motion; positioning; turning and repositioning
Module 9 - Elimination (3 hrs theory / 10 hrs clinical): bowel and bladder care; catheter care; ostomy care; documenting elimination
Module 10 - Vital Signs (3 hrs theory / 6 hrs clinical): taking and recording temperature, pulse, respirations, blood pressure; recognizing abnormal values and reporting to supervisor

Module 11 - Mental Health and Social Service Needs (2 hrs theory / 3 hrs clinical): behavior modification; aging process; responding to resident behavior; supporting resident dignity and autonomy; family involvement

Module 12 - Cognitive Impairment (4 hrs theory / 4 hrs clinical, including at least 4 hrs clinical for developmental/mental disorders): dementia and Alzheimer's care; communication with cognitively impaired residents; appropriate behavioral responses; reducing effects of cognitive impairment; special needs of persons with developmental and mental disorders including cerebral palsy, epilepsy, Parkinson's disease, and mental illness

Module 13 - Basic Restorative Care (3 hrs theory / 6 hrs clinical): self-care training per resident ability; assistive devices for transferring, ambulation, eating, and dressing; maintenance of range of motion; bowel and bladder training; proper turning and positioning

Module 14 - Observation, Documentation and Reporting (3 hrs theory / 3 hrs clinical): observing and recording changes in resident condition; reporting to supervisor; care plan documentation; legal aspects of documentation
Module 15 - Medical and Surgical Asepsis (2 hrs theory / 4 hrs clinical): principles of asepsis; sterile technique; wound care support; handling of medical equipment
Module 16 - Death and Dying (1 hr theory / 4 hrs clinical): emotional needs of dying residents and families; signs of approaching death; care of a resident who is dying; postmortem care

CNA Annual In-Service Training: 24 hours of varied in-service training per year. Content must address: areas of weakness from performance reviews; special needs of patients with cognitive needs; deficiencies cited in last licensing survey. Includes 4 hours of resident abuse training every 2 years.
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: Facility must submit in-service schedule for CDPH approval. Topics must include multiple subjects. Shall address patient special needs and survey deficiency areas. 4-hr resident abuse training is a mandatory sub-requirement on a 2-year cycle. | Per §71847(f)(15), infection control is an explicitly enumerated in-service topic: universal precautions; handling patients and materials soiled with blood/body fluids; methods to reduce transmission of infectious agents.

CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: Overarching training mandate. All specific topics at §483.95(a)–(i) fall under this umbrella. Training topics must include but are not limited to the enumerated items below.

CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Communication: effective communications training mandatory for all direct care staff
Resident Rights and Facility Responsibilities: staff must be educated on the rights of the resident per §483.10 and the facility's responsibilities for proper resident care

Abuse, Neglect, and Exploitation Training: training must educate staff on - (1) what constitutes abuse, neglect, exploitation, and misappropriation of resident property; (2) procedures for reporting; (3) the facility's policies prohibiting and preventing abuse
QAPI Training: mandatory training that outlines and informs staff of the elements and goals of the facility's Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) program
Infection Control Training: mandatory training that includes the facility's written standards, policies, and procedures for the infection prevention and control program

CS SNF.Jurisdiction Role: All staff, managers, and (where applicable) governing body
CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Compliance and Ethics Training: facility operating organization must include an effective way to communicate compliance and ethics program standards, policies, and procedures. Annual training required for organizations operating 5 or more facilities.

Nurse Aide Annual In-Service Training: facility must provide regular in-service training based on outcome of annual performance reviews. Must address areas of weakness identified in reviews; facility assessment; and, for aides serving cognitively impaired residents, care of the cognitively impaired.
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: 12-hour annual minimum is the federal standard per §483.95(g)(2). CA exceeds this with 24 hrs. Must address performance review deficiencies and cognitive impairment care for applicable staff.

CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Paid Feeding Assistant Training: facility must not use any individual as a paid feeding assistant unless that individual has successfully completed a state-approved training program for feeding assistants per §483.160
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: State-approved feeding assistant programs required. Content must include: feeding techniques; assistance with eating and hydration; communication; safety; and recognizing resident distress.

CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Behavioral Health Training: facility must provide behavioral health training consistent with the requirements at §483.40 and the facility assessment. Trauma-informed care is an explicit component per 2024 regulatory guidance.
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: 2024 CMS guidance (89 FR 41000, May 10, 2024) strengthened trauma-informed care expectations within §483.95(i). Nine F-tags now cover TIC-related requirements. High-priority content area given survey exposure.

CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Nurse Aide Training and Competency Evaluation Program (NATCEP): minimum 75 clock hours including at least 16 hours supervised practical training. Must include all subjects in §483.152(b). Must complete competency evaluation (written/oral + skills demonstration) within 4 months of employment.
CS SNF.Approval Required: Yes - state-approved program; competency evaluation required
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: Federal minimum floor. States may (and most do) require more hours. CA requires 160 hrs. FL aligns with §464 F.S. Competency evaluation required before independent practice. Facility may not charge employed aides for training costs.

CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: NATCEP Pre-Contact Curriculum (16 hours minimum before any resident contact): (i) communication and interpersonal skills; (ii) infection control; (iii) safety/emergency procedures including Heimlich maneuver; (iv) promoting residents' independence; (v) respecting residents' rights
CS SNF.Frequency: Prior to any direct resident contact

CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: NATCEP Curriculum - Basic Nursing Skills: taking and recording vital signs; measuring and recording height and weight; caring for the resident's environment; recognizing abnormal changes in body functioning and reporting to supervisor; caring for residents when death is imminent

NATCEP Curriculum - Personal Care Skills: bathing; grooming including mouth care; dressing; toileting; assisting with eating and hydration; proper feeding techniques; skin care; transfers, positioning, and turning

NATCEP Curriculum - Mental Health and Social Service Needs: modifying aide's behavior in response to resident behavior; awareness of developmental tasks associated with aging; how to respond to resident behavior; allowing resident personal choices while supporting dignity; using resident's family as a source of emotional support

NATCEP Curriculum - Care of Cognitively Impaired Residents: techniques for addressing unique needs and behaviors of individuals with dementia (Alzheimer's and others); communicating with cognitively impaired residents; understanding cognitively impaired resident behavior; appropriate responses; methods of reducing effects of cognitive impairment

NATCEP Curriculum - Basic Restorative Services: training the resident in self-care per abilities; use of assistive devices in transferring, ambulation, eating, and dressing; maintenance of range of motion; proper turning and positioning in bed and chair; bowel and bladder training; care and use of prosthetic and orthotic devices

NATCEP Curriculum - Residents' Rights: including the right to be free from verbal, sexual, physical, and mental abuse, corporal punishment, and involuntary seclusion; the right to privacy and confidentiality; making a complaint; and the rights of married residents

CS SNF.Jurisdiction Role: All new and existing staff, individuals providing services under arrangement
CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Emergency Preparedness Training and Testing: facility must provide initial training in emergency preparedness policies and procedures to all new and existing staff and individuals providing services under arrangement. Annual training required thereafter. Must also conduct drills and exercises per §483.73(d)(2).
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: Emergency preparedness is a standalone Condition of Participation. Includes tabletop exercises and/or full-scale drills. Documentation of training participation required.

CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Infection Preventionist (IP) Role Training: facility must designate a point of contact for infection control with specialized training. IP must be qualified through education, training, experience, or certification. Training must address the facility's written IPCP standards and procedures.
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: IP must have sufficient training and knowledge per §483.80(b). AHCA IPCO certification is the industry-standard program used to meet this requirement. High F-tag exposure area. | ⚠️ QA FLAG: No specialist HSTM audience category exists for Infection Preventionist. Mapped to 'Clinical, Non-Medication Dispensing' as interim. Recommend creating a dedicated IP/Specialist audience bucket in HSTM taxonomy.

CS SNF.Jurisdiction Role: Facility senior leadership and quality improvement teams
CS SNF.Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
CS SNF.Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program - Program Overview: a voluntary three-level quality recognition program for long-term care organizations,  based on the Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework. Designed to evaluate organizational strengths, identify improvement opportunities, and drive excellence in clinical and operational outcomes beyond minimum regulatory compliance. Bronze requires foundational process deployment; Silver requires systematic approach alignment across the organization; Gold requires advanced integration of approaches and sustained, benchmarked results across all 7 Baldrige categories.
CS SNF.Hours Required: 0 (facility-determined; significant preparation investment at Silver and Gold levels)
CS SNF.Frequency: Annual application cycle (award levels are cumulative)
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: Not a training mandate - a quality recognition framework. Inclusion in this tracker reflects HealthStream product positioning opportunity: facilities actively pursuing AHCA/NCAL award levels require structured workforce development activities across all 7 Baldrige categories, representing above-compliance training investment. Award-seeking facilities are high-propensity buyers for competency-based learning content. AHCA describes this framework as the basis for evaluating 'strengths, opportunities, and improvement in clinical and operational outcomes.'

CS SNF.Jurisdiction Role: Senior leadership (Administrator, Director of Nursing, Department Heads)
CS SNF.Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
CS SNF.Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Leadership: senior leaders must define, communicate, and deploy organizational values, vision, and mission; create and sustain a culture of resident-centered excellence and ethical behavior; and personally lead organizational learning and improvement. Requires evidence of leader visibility, accountability systems, two-way communication with workforce and residents, and governance oversight. SNF application: administrator and DON modeling evidence-based leadership behaviors, setting and cascading quality goals, ensuring regulatory and ethical accountability, and creating a culture of safety and improvement.
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 1 of 7. Directly maps to HealthStream leadership development content: servant leadership, change management, culture of safety, and ethical decision-making for long-term care leaders.

CS SNF.Jurisdiction Role: Senior leadership and quality improvement teams
CS SNF.Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
CS SNF.Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Strategy: the organization develops strategic objectives and action plans aligned with resident needs, workforce capabilities, regulatory environment, and competitive landscape. Requires data-informed goal-setting, deployment of strategic plans across all operational units, and measurement of progress against stated goals. SNF application: quality strategic planning cycles, regulatory compliance roadmaps, workforce development prioritization, Five-Star improvement planning, and alignment of organizational goals with AHCA quality initiatives.
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 2 of 7. Maps to HealthStream content around healthcare quality strategy, QAPI program design (which overlaps with CMS §483.75), and strategic performance management for long-term care leaders.

CS SNF.Jurisdiction Role: All staff with resident and family contact
CS SNF.Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
CS SNF.Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Customers (Residents and Families): the organization systematically listens to and engages residents, families, and key stakeholders; identifies needs, preferences, and expectations; and builds relationships that support satisfaction, loyalty, and service recovery. Requires structured feedback mechanisms, complaint resolution processes, and customer segmentation by care need. SNF application: resident-centered care delivery, satisfaction survey administration and action planning, family engagement protocols, grievance resolution systems, and individualized care preference documentation.
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 3 of 7. Broadest audience applicability - all direct care staff contribute to resident and family experience. Maps to HealthStream person-centered care, communication, and customer service content. Strong overlap with CMS requirements at §483.10 (Resident Rights) and §483.95(b), but Baldrige approach is systematic and outcome-driven rather than compliance-minimum.

CS SNF.Jurisdiction Role: Quality improvement staff, administrative and clinical leadership
CS SNF.Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
CS SNF.Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Measurement, Analysis, and Knowledge Management: the organization selects, collects, aligns, and uses data and information for performance tracking and improvement decisions. Requires reliable performance measurement systems, comparative benchmarking against industry standards, data integrity processes, and organizational knowledge-sharing mechanisms. SNF application: QM/QI indicator tracking, MDS data analysis and validation, Five-Star Quality Rating driver analysis, CMS Care Compare benchmarking, NHSN infection data reporting, LTC Trend Tracker use, and internal quality dashboard design and deployment.
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 4 of 7. Maps to HealthStream content around QI fundamentals, data literacy for clinical leaders, MDS accuracy, and QAPI program execution. Highest overlap with CMS QAPI requirements at §483.75 and §483.95(d) - Baldrige Category 4 represents the systematic, above-compliance version of the federal QAPI mandate.

CS SNF.Jurisdiction Role: All staff; HR, education, and workforce development leadership
CS SNF.Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
CS SNF.Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Workforce: the organization builds a capable, engaged, and high-performing workforce through systems for workforce capability assessment, learning and development, performance management, and employee well-being and satisfaction. Requires structured competency development programs, onboarding quality, engagement measurement, and workforce planning aligned with organizational strategy. SNF application: competency-based training systems, new hire onboarding effectiveness, staff engagement and retention strategies, performance evaluation processes, career ladder development, and learning culture assessment.
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 5 of 7. The most direct alignment with HealthStream's core product value proposition. Category 5 is essentially a structured framework for the workforce development investment HealthStream enables. Award-seeking facilities need to demonstrate systematic, measured competency development programs.

CS SNF.Jurisdiction Role: Clinical and operational leadership; department heads
CS SNF.Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
CS SNF.Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Operations: the organization designs, manages, and continuously improves work systems and processes to deliver safe, high-quality, and efficient care and services. Requires process standardization, performance measurement at the process level, emergency preparedness integration, supply chain management, and cross-functional coordination. SNF application: clinical care delivery workflow design, medication management systems, infection prevention program management, fall prevention process standardization, care coordination between disciplines, and emergency/disaster preparedness program integration.
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 6 of 7. Maps to HealthStream content in clinical operations, infection control, medication management, and emergency preparedness. Significant overlap with CMS §483.80 (IPCP), §483.45 (Pharmacy), and §483.73 (Emergency Preparedness).

CS SNF.Jurisdiction Role: Senior leadership and quality improvement teams
CS SNF.Oversight / Professional Agency: AHCA/NCAL (American Health Care Association / National Center for Assisted Living)
CS SNF.Citation: AHCA/NCAL National Quality Award Program; Baldrige Performance Excellence Framework
CS SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Results: the organization demonstrates sustained performance and measurable improvement across all key result areas - clinical/health outcomes, resident and family satisfaction, workforce outcomes, operational and process performance, leadership and governance, and financial/market performance. Requires trended data across multiple measurement periods, benchmarking against comparable organizations, and demonstration of cause-and-effect linkage between approaches (Categories 1–6) and results. SNF application: Five-Star Quality Rating trajectory, CMS QM scores, NHSN HAI and infection data, staff turnover and retention rates, survey deficiency trend analysis, resident and family satisfaction scores (AHCA/NCAL LTC Trend Tracker), and operating margin performance.
CS SNF.Notes / Research Flags: Baldrige Category 7 of 7. Results category is the capstone - Gold-level applicants must demonstrate results across all seven categories with multi-year trend data and industry benchmarks. Direct alignment with Five-Star Quality Rating system: staffing domain maps to Category 5 results, health inspection domain maps to Category 6 results, QM domain maps to Categories 3–4 results.
